enhanced_information: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is typically an opportunistic pathogen, commonly found in soil and water, known for antibiotic resistance. It is not sensitive to most antibiotics used in human medicine. It is not a commensal bacteria of the digestive tract or an intracellular pathogen. Evidence paths confirm its role in causing infections like sinusitis and endocarditis.
analysis: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is typically known as an opportunistic pathogen, commonly found in soil and water, and is notorious for its antibiotic resistance. It is not sensitive to most antibiotics used in human medicine. It is associated with causing infections like sinusitis and endocarditis.
